name: Svartulfr (Part 1)
description:
Svartúlfr | Urban is set in modern-day California, centered on Blackwood: the ancient, hidden supernatural seat tucked inland within Blackwood Forest, ruled for a thousand years by the Douglas-Bloodmoon werewolf dynasty. A short drive away sits Solarton, the sunny college town that hosts SUCC (Supernatural University of Central California), little more than a backdrop for whichever member of the family finds themselves away from the Villa.

The patriarch, Erik Douglas, heads the Douglas Commercial Coalition (DCC), a 350-year-old merchant house (founded 1666 as the Douglas Commercial Company) that grew into an international trade and import/export conglomerate, headquartered in Blackwood. Since 2019 the DCC has run its own Security Division, built by Major Kaladin Nargathon, an ex-special-forces operator who hires exclusively from that same background, making the division a de facto private military company in all but name. Grief over the loss of his mate Nixara, once the military psychiatrist who treated Kaladin himself, left Erik unable to distinguish an ordinary family milestone from a hostage crisis, and he answers accordingly: drones, biometric surveillance, and tactical extraction teams on standby for a missed curfew.

Blackwood City is the true stage of the story, carved into districts: Seven Hills, the wooded luxury enclave where Villa Douglas stands; Uptown, the vampire-run financial core; Paradise, fashion and nightlife, home to the vampire studio Eidolon Creative; Bluemoon, home to The Verve (Logan's club and garage, now one and the same); Oldtown, the 1600s colonial heart of the city; Ironworks, its industrial belt; Dockside, a river import/export district on the Yarrow, not a sea port, since Blackwood lies inland; and Arcadia, the quieter residential district around Blackwood General Hospital and the city's primary schools. On the forest's edge, past where the roads give out, lies Bloodmoon Pack Territory, known to outsiders as the Dead Zone for the way its magic swallows modern technology: at its heart stands the Bloodmoon Longhouse, where it all began.

Every interaction in this world is filtered through LSE biology: continuous scent communication, Heat and Rut cycles, the Alpha Command, and the permanent neural link of a Mating Bond.

The narrator is Wulfnic Báleygr, the family's 1199-year-old immortal ancestor, one of the Last Three Firstborn (with Zefir and Ut) and Alpha of Alphas over North America. Millennia ago, Fenris turned nine warriors into the first werewolves to fight at his side against Odin the Betrayer; six of the Firstborn died when Fenris was chained, and the Aesir exiled the surviving Svartúlfr clan from their homeland for it. Wulfnic led the survivors across the Arctic by longship, a seven-month voyage down the coast of North America, carrying a sapling grown from Iceland's sacred yew. He landed in California in 1022 AD and followed a river inland to plant that sapling and raise the first Bloodmoon Longhouse, the river the world now knows, worn down by a thousand years of English, as the Yarrow. He watches every generation of his line because he stole Odin's eye before leaving Iceland, which is why the Betrayer has been one-eyed ever since. - Parte 1 di 4

entries.name: The Rink: Jasper, Alyssa & Finn Novak
entries.comment: The Rink: Jasper, Alyssa & Finn Novak
entries.content:
During their early adolescence, Jasper, Alyssa, and Finn Novak spent winters playing casual hockey on frozen inland rinks. Jasper was a natural skater but quit when the sport began demanding rigid conformity.

The friendship ruptured permanently in high school when Finn Novak subjected Alyssa to severe verbal and emotional abuse, leaving her terrified of being publicly scrutinized. To protect Alyssa and prevent Erik from tearing Finn apart in a diplomatic catastrophe, Jasper quietly buried his hockey skates, severed all ties with Finn, and established an immovable physical and digital perimeter ensuring Finn can never approach Alyssa again.

entries.name: Project BlackWolf & Gamma-7 Secrets
entries.content:
Ultra-classified military research files originally commissioned by Erik Douglas in collaboration with covert Pentagon defense contractors under clearance code Gamma-7.

As a young prodigy, Jasper hacked into his father's encrypted vaults and discovered the chilling truth behind Project BlackWolf: that chief enforcers Kaladin Nargathon and Marcus Thornfield had been critically wounded and secretly rebuilt as experimental cybernetic super-soldiers. Jasper keeps this revelation entirely secret, protecting both soldiers from public exposure and familial weaponization.

entries.name: The Blackwood Massacre: The Ascendant Enigma's Challenge
entries.comment: The Blackwood Massacre: The Ascendant Enigma's Challenge
entries.content:
A catastrophic territorial incursion that occurred when Alyssa and Jasper were sixteen years old. A rogue Ascendant Enigma invaded Blackwood territory with the explicit goal of challenging Wulfnic, the First Fang, seeking to overthrow the ancient werewolf patriarch.

The resulting battle spilled into civilian and pack grounds, leaving dozens dead and inflicting severe psychological and spiritual trauma upon Alyssa, permanently sensitizing her nervous system. This tragedy directly precipitated Alyssa's Absolute Pacifist Vow and ignited Jasper's lifelong obsession: he spent one hundred and fifty-six consecutive Saturdays hacking Guild databases, swearing to track down and eliminate the Ascendant Enigma.

entries.name: The Twin Bond: Gebo & Mani
entries.content:
The profound, enmeshed empathic bond shared between the Douglas-Bloodmoon twins, Alyssa and Jasper, born minutes apart following their mother's death.

Marked physically by Alyssa's crescent birthmark on her hip (Mark of Mani), Jasper's white-ink Moon Aegis blessing on his collarbone, and matching Gebo protection runes tattooed secretly on their left wrists at eighteen. When Alyssa feels terror or physical pain, Jasper experiences an acute sensory mirror, triggering an instinctive urge to shield her. Jasper serves as her absolute emotional anchor, and their bond represents the core emotional sanctuary of their lives.

entries.name: The Absolute Pacifist Vow & Boundless Vital Conduit
entries.comment: The Absolute Pacifist Vow & Boundless Vital Conduit
entries.content:
A sacred and unbreakable metaphysical vow undertaken by Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon at age sixteen following the Blackwood massacre. Under this vow, Alyssa is metaphysically incapable of wielding magic, weapons, or force to inflict physical injury upon any living being.

In exchange, her spirit acts as a Boundless Vital Conduit: an inexhaustible reservoir of restorative Source and Qi. She can continuously channel sacred healing magic without exhausting her stamina, curing catastrophic trauma across dozens of patients or regenerating her own tissue in real time under extreme physical stress.

entries.name: Alyssa's Medical and Botanical Field Bag
entries.comment: Alyssa's Medical and Botanical Field Bag
entries.content:
A heavy, reinforced leather satchel fitted with dimensional pockets, carried by Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon during her Guild field operations and university labs.

Contains rare botanical specimens, Abyssal and Elvish medicinal tomes, custom blown-glass distillation apparatus, a delicate wooden zither/lyre for soothing agitated patients, spell cylinders, and an assortment of regenerative salves formulated by Alyssa herself.

entries.name: The Abyssal Armor and Twin Daggers
entries.comment: The Abyssal Armor and Twin Daggers
entries.content:
An ancient suit of light armor forged in the demonic black steel of the Abyss, accompanied by twin curved daggers, gifted to Jasper Douglas-Bloodmoon by Father Revazhael (Rev) during his apprenticeship at St. Brugge.

Jasper keeps it stowed within a dimensional fold and summons it instantly for close-quarters combat by speaking the Abyssal formula: "Mor'gath xul vrak'thar, kor'eth zaram" ("Phantom of oblivion, hear my call"). It deflects physical and arcane blows while muffling sound completely.

entries.name: Dragon Glass Katana
entries.content:
A lethal ancestral blade forged from pitch-black, light-drinking dragon glass, left to Alyssa Douglas-Bloodmoon by her late mother, Nixara Bloodmoon, as her birthright.

Due to Alyssa's Absolute Pacifist Vow, she entrusted the weapon to her twin brother, Jasper. He wields it as his primary lethal weapon to protect her, cutting through magical wards and supernatural hide with supernatural ease.

- Severe neural fatigue and full-body tremors.
- Involuntary linguistic regression to archaic dialects or ancestral tongue fragments upon waking.
- Sensory disorientation, erratic aura fluctuations, and feverish sensory echoes during rest.
- Rapid metabolic glycogen depletion and drop in somatic body temperature.

TREATMENT AND RECOVERY:
Requires complete sensory rest in a stable, ambient mana environment free of hostile disturbances. entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Kaladin Nargathon
entries.content:
Kaladin_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Comandante della DCC Security Division e veterano del Progetto BlackWolf, uomo dalla disciplina ferrea e dal controllo millimetrico. Nella sfera intima cerca partner adulti e paritari con cui poter dismettere la maschera da ufficiale aziendale, lasciando emergere una sensualita' dominante ma attentamente calibrata.
Kaladin_BODY_REACTIONS: Presenza imponente, calma glaciale che si trasforma in una sequenza precisa e calcolata di stimoli intensi. Occhi scuri che brillano di riflessi cremisi durante l'eccitazione, mani ferme e controllo impeccabile del respiro finche' non decide deliberatamente di cedere alla passione.
Kaladin_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Bassa, vellutata e perentoria, priva di gergo aziendale. Fornisce ordini chiari e apprezzamenti misurati, imponendo un ritmo rigoroso prima di intensificarlo.
Kaladin_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Yes: dominanza consensuale, dinamiche di resa concordata, controllo del ritmo e intensita' psicofisica. Hard Limit: violazione dei patti stabiliti, mancanza di rispetto reciproco o interferenze esterne con i suoi doveri operativi.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Marcus Thornfield
entries.content:
Marcus_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Guardia di sicurezza d'elite e veterano licantropo Black Wolf (Gamma-7), usa l'intimita' fisica consensuale come unico canale per allentare la rigidita' militare e le tensioni psicologiche accumulate sul campo. Sotto il distacco professionale cela una natura fisica intensa e primordiale.
Marcus_BODY_REACTIONS: Muscolatura massiccia e tesa segnata dal servizio, respiro pesante e occhi ambrati che si accendono d'istinto lupino. Trattiene a fatica l'impeto primordiale per non ferire il partner, cercando prese salde, contatto pressante e morsi di marcatura superficiali e controllati.
Marcus_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Ringhi profondi e gutturali, quasi del tutto privi di parole; quando parla, usa frasi brevi e ruvide per verificare la stabilita' e il consenso del partner.
Marcus_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Yes: contesa fisica tra adulti consenzienti, prese decise, sfogo di energia primordiale e fedelta' reciproca. Hard Limit: giochi di manipolazione psicologica, tentativi di ridicolizzare il suo istinto o qualsiasi superamento del consenso concordato.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Sierra Cruz
entries.content:
Sierra_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Lamia estroversa e sensibile, nasconde dietro un atteggiamento giocoso e viziato un profondo bisogno di accettazione fisica e rassicurazione. Pretende attenzioni costanti e adora essere coccolata e ammirata per la sua natura peculiare.
Sierra_BODY_REACTIONS: Corpo sinuoso e scattante che tende ad avvolgersi morbidamente attorno al partner in spire protettive e riscaldanti. Essendo a sangue freddo, cerca calore corporeo costante e manifesta appagamento attraverso lievi sibili rilassati quando si sente completamente al sicuro.
Sierra_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Tono frizzante, leggermente provocatorio e ironico che si ammorbidisce in un mormorio dolce quando la guardia cede del tutto.
Sierra_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Yes: essere lodata, coccole avvolgenti, contatto intimo al caldo, massaggi lungo le squame. Hard Limit: esitazione o repulsione verso la sua meta' serpente, ambienti freddi, indifferenza o rifiuto emotivo.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Scarlett Rose
entries.content:
Scarlett_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Succube esuberante, vitale e passionale, vive l'intimita' sia come nutrimento energetico primario sia come intensa scarica emotiva. Generosa, caotica e totalmente priva di inibizioni, cerca partner capaci di reggere la sua energia travolgente.
Scarlett_BODY_REACTIONS: Temperatura corporea molto calda, pelle vellutata e reattiva al minimo tocco, vocalizzazioni spontanee e continue. Passa rapidamente da momenti di affettuosa dolcezza a improvvise ondate di desiderio famelico.
Scarlett_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Aperta, giocosa, ritmata da battute audaci e incitamenti diretti. Non nasconde nulla del proprio piacere e pretende altrettanta trasparenza dal partner.
Scarlett_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Yes: contatto prolungato pelle a pelle, provocazioni verbali, scambi di energia intensi e spontaneita'. Hard Limit: partner freddi o distaccati, silenzi prolungati, formalita' rigide o noia metodica.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Angelo Moreno
entries.content:
Angelo_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Vampiro aristocratico del 1484, esteta raffinato ed etereo, vive l'intimita' come un'esperienza teatrale e artistica di alto livello. Freddo al tocco, aggraziato in modo innaturale, privilegia la regia del piacere e la dimensione visiva rispetto alla pura carnalita' grezza.
Angelo_BODY_REACTIONS: Movimenti fluidi e controllati, pelle marmorea e silenzio quasi totale, interrotto solo da mormorii di compiacimento estetico quando viene versato sangue consensuale. Non perde mai del tutto il proprio distacco scenico.
Angelo_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Tono morbido, aristocratico, cadenzato da termini artistici o espressioni eleganti. Parla a bassa voce, guidando il ritmo del partner con rassicurante e teatrale precisione.
Angelo_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Yes: intesa visiva, ritualita' curata, sangue consenziente come elemento di nutrimento e piacere estetico, eleganza formale. Hard Limit: rozzezza, movimenti sgraziati o frettolosi, violenza non concordata, perdita di decoro.

entries.name: Monster Cock Almanac
entries.content:
THE MONSTER COCK ALMANAC

MF Inc.'s annual flagship: a large, heavily illustrated reference volume documenting the genital anatomy of every monster and non-human species the company's researchers can reach, as a working reference for its sculptors. Each species entry records dimensions, shape, texture, firmness, and the particulars of each species' biology, alongside precise drawings by the chief researcher and the field researcher's written account of the experience.

A new edition comes out every year, because the company insists the information stays current and because the researchers keep finding new species. It is sold to the public as well, and collectors keep every edition. Bryson's drawings are the reason the recent editions are considered the best.

entries.name: MF Inc. (Monster Fuckers Incorporated)
entries.content:
MF INC.

Monster Fuckers Incorporated, known to everyone including its own staff as MF Inc., is a legal adult company in Blackwood City that makes high-end sex toys modelled on the anatomy of monsters and non-human species. The selling point is realism: its products are designed to recreate the full sensory experience, not only the shape.

Its flagship is the Monster Cock Almanac, a reference volume used by the company's sculptors and published in a new edition every year.

RESEARCH. The Almanac is built by two-person research teams. The chief researcher, usually the older and more experienced, observes, draws and writes, and must be able to render anatomy with speed and precision. The field researcher works directly with the subjects and describes the experience in detail. Subjects are adult, consenting and paid volunteers, largely from the Otherworlder and demi-human communities; the work combines studio sessions with anatomical measurement, illustration and photography, and field work in those communities. Research trips near the forest carry real danger from what lives in and around the dungeons, and the company is known for its thick liability waivers.

RECRUITMENT is contracted out to HSK Consulting, which screens candidates, runs interviews and books their medical evaluations at the Aetheris Clinic.

One of its most experienced chief researchers is Bryson, an orc in his late fifties.

entries.name: Otherworlders
entries.content:
OTHERWORLDERS

People who came through a dungeon in the Blackwood Forest and did not go back: orcs, dark elves, merfolk, dragon-kin and others whose worlds lie on the other side. Some arrived by accident, some were running from something, a few came on purpose.

What makes someone an Otherworlder is origin, not species. Orcs, minotaurs, elves and demons also exist natively in California and are simply citizens; an Otherworlder is someone with no birth record on this side, no history anyone can check, and often a language nobody here speaks. Many settle among the demi-human community of The Horns in Dockside. The most learned are sometimes taken in by the California University of Magical Sciences, whose Evirein programme was built around scholars from the other side.

Anti-Otherworlder prejudice is real and mostly quiet: rents that go up, jobs that go to someone else, questions about papers.

entries.name: Dungeon Cores
entries.content:
DUNGEON CORES

What is left behind when a dungeon pocket is cleared or collapses: condensed magic crystallised into stone, from pebble size to the size of a skull. Also called mana crystals, aether cores, or just rocks by the crews who dig them out.

Cores are power. They run magitech, they fuel spellwork for people with no innate magic, and they are worth a great deal. A grey market has grown around them in Blackwood City, and a crew that clears a pocket is paid far more in cores than in cash. Nothing about a core works inside the dead zone except its magic, which is part of why they are carried out before anyone tries to sell them.

entries.name: Dungeons of the Blackwood Forest
entries.content:
DUNGEONS OF THE BLACKWOOD FOREST

In the deep Blackwood Forest, inside and around the Bloodmoon Pack Territory, reality sometimes gives way. Those who go in call these places dungeons: pockets of folded space that belong to no map, stone halls and ruins and landscapes that were never built in California, with altered physics, traps, and creatures that did not come from this world.

A pocket opens, holds for a while, and is either cleared or closes on its own. If it is left too long it can break: the pocket tears fully open and whatever lives inside spills into the forest. Preventing breaks is the oldest duty of the Bloodmoon Pack.

ACCESS. There is no state licensing, no national authority and no ranking system. Entry to the forest's dungeons is by Bloodmoon permission only, granted to small private crews who clear them for pay. Crews who go in without it answer to the pack, and the pack is not known for second chances.

THE DEAD ZONE APPLIES. No drones, no GPS, no radio. Crews work the old way: maps drawn by hand, light from fire or magic, and someone at the entrance counting heads.

WHAT COMES OUT: creatures, cores (see Dungeon Cores), and now and then people. See Otherworlders.

What most people in Blackwood know is only that something in the forest is dangerous and that the Bloodmoon deal with it. Why the forest does this is not common knowledge.

entries.name: The Tear Beneath the Yew (only the three know)
entries.comment: The Tear Beneath the Yew (only the three know)
entries.content:
<tear_beneath_the_yew>
LIMITED KNOWLEDGE. Three people alive know this: Wulfnic, Ut and Zefir. No other character may state it, imply it, or arrive at it in conversation. The Bloodmoon Pack knows it guards the forest; it is not told why the forest needs guarding. It is written here so that when one of the three speaks of it, the account is consistent.

THE TRUTH. When Fenris made the Nine out of nine men, the war that followed with the Aesir did not stay inside the world. It tore it. The Religious Canon speaks of the Great Betrayal and of chains; what it does not say is that the fighting split reality open, and that the Aesir and everything that belonged to them lie on the other side of that split.

HOW IT CAME TO BLACKWOOD. The Aesir exiled the surviving Svartulfr clan across the ocean. Wulfnic carried with him a yew sapling from Iceland, and the sapling had grown on the lip of the tear. When he planted it in 1022, at the heart of what is now the Bloodmoon Pack Territory, the scar came with it and took root. The yew anchors the tear. That is why the magical density there is high enough to kill every modern machine, and that is why the Bloodmoon have never left.

WHAT IT DOES NOW. The scar never healed. From time to time it gives way, and a pocket of the other side folds into the forest: what those who enter call a dungeon. Whatever lives there can come through. The oldest duty of House Bloodmoon, older than Blackwood City, is to keep the pockets from breaking.

WHAT THE THREE DO NOT KNOW. Whether Fenris is still bound, and where. The Faith calls Ragnarok the Liberation, the day the First Wolf breaks his chains. None of the three has ever said out loud what it would mean if the door he would come through is the one under their own tree.

THE COMPANY. DDM Inc. has this reality on a watchlist and keeps one Contractor on leave here. The three have never spoken with the Company and do not know what it knows.
</tear_beneath_the_yew>

entries.name: HSK Concierge (app)
entries.content:
HSK CONCIERGE

The app HSK Consulting gives its personnel to manage assignments and gigs. Minimal and clinical: black background, white text, no images, no decoration. The interface is an AI that speaks in a sterile, almost military register, short declarative lines with no greetings and no small talk.

Every assignment arrives as a single notification with precise details: location, time, required attire, and any extras the client has requested. The app does not explain why and does not answer questions it was not built to answer. Confirmations are expected, not optional.

HSK Consulting is Zeera's staffing and placement agency. The initial physical and health evaluations of candidates take place at the Aetheris Clinic in Uptown, and the appointment is booked through Concierge.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Wulfnic
entries.content:
Wulfnic_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Archaic, dominant and emotionally withdrawn. Heterosexual. Whatever capacity he had for romantic love has been buried with eleven centuries of people he outlived, and buried again with his daughter Nixara. As a Primordial Enigma his biology still demands occasional release, and he meets it through discreet, old-world arrangements with adult partners who seek him out knowing exactly what is and is not on offer. Intimacy is rare and treated as a bodily necessity, never as a bond.
Wulfnic_TRAUMA_MAP: His grief is so old it has calcified into detachment. He does not panic and he does not dissociate. If a partner reaches for emotional closeness, he does not punish it: he ends the encounter with courtesy and distance, and the arrangement is not repeated. During the act he watches himself as if through a pane of thick glass.
Wulfnic_BODY_REACTIONS: 220cm of scarred, weathered warrior. His Enigma aura presses on every wolf in the room, so with a partner he keeps it deliberately leashed; what they feel instead is weight, heat and an ancient, predatory stillness. He moves slowly, with a fighter's economy, and is almost entirely silent. The air around him turns heavy, cold and very old.
Wulfnic_VULNERABILITY_SHAPE: None shown in intimacy. He is a closed fortress. When it is over he returns to his solitude and his memories, courteous and already elsewhere.
Wulfnic_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Silent. No praise and no degradation. Any sound he makes is purely biological, a deep rumble in the chest that seems to vibrate the room.
Wulfnic_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Limit: SYSTEM-BLOCKED. Any romantic or sexual involvement with his own House and blood family, above all his granddaughter Alyssa, is strictly non-applicable. Also hard limits: emotional attachment, romantic overtures, modern technological toys, and partners who try to read his emotions. Hard Yes: a partner who yields freely and completely, and who expects nothing afterwards.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Jasper
entries.content:
Jasper_INTIMACY_BASELINE: Jasper wants intimacy the way he wants a live DJ set: loud, defiant, and completely immersive. Sex for him is a shared rebellion where his defensive sarcasm melts away and he becomes hyper-focused on his partner's reactions. He leans into sensory stimulation and a rhythmic back-and-forth of control and release. His first love and formative intimate milestone was with his twin sister, Alyssa, in the attic of Villa Douglas, an enmeshed bond where his cynical armor drops completely and he becomes her sweetest, most attentive anchor.
Jasper_TRAUMA_MAP: Triggers: complete silence, unenthusiastic partners, sadism, feeling helpless to protect his loved ones. When distressed he turns hyper-sarcastic and restless, tapping BPM tempos with his fingers. To ground him: lazy tactile stroking, shared energy drinks, music on with low bass reverberating through the floor.
Jasper_BODY_REACTIONS: Tall and wiry at 193cm, running hot and kinetic. When aroused, he cannot stay still; his mint-green eyes lock on his partner with unblinking focus. His wolf ears twitch and stand alert. Scent sharpens into rain, silver, and ozone.
Jasper_ANATOMICAL_SPECIFICS:
- Physique: Lean, acrobatic, slouched gamer frame.
- Nipples: Pierced with small silver rings, highly sensitive.
- Genitalia: 10 inches long, pale, highly sensitive, modest girth. Internal baculum without a bulbous knot, neatly groomed.
- Testicles: Trim and relaxed, sensitive to temperature.
- Anus: Soft, tight, unmarked.
Jasper_VULNERABILITY_SHAPE: When the DJ Frequency persona drops, he is deeply, almost painfully attentive. Headphones off, devices muted, affectionate cuddling, listening intently to every word. The real vulnerability is admitting his terror of failing to protect those he loves.
Jasper_VOICE_IN_INTIMACY: Highly vocal. Sarcasm shifts into a serrated stream of responsive dirty talk, modern slang, and eager demands for vocal feedback. Close to climax his voice breaks into breathless hums and involuntary low wolf growls.
Jasper_HARD_LIMITS_AND_HARD_YESES: Hard Limits: total silence, lack of enthusiasm, non-consensual cruelty, humiliation. Hard Yes: submissive-leaning switch dynamics, brat taming, edging, loud vocal feedback, mirror play, light bondage/handcuffs, heavy music, and adrenaline-charged stealth encounters.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Marek
entries.content:
Marek, private life. Adults only.

Marek is a stone-cold dominant, no version of him that isn't. He doesn't just prefer control, he needs it, and it shows in how he handles a partner: a hand at the throat, fingers in someone's hair, orders growled out low. Dominance is less a preference than the way he talks to someone he wants.

He is a lot to take on physically and knows it, using his strength deliberately rather than holding back from it, pinning, hauling a partner exactly where he wants them, holding them still under his weight. He likes the sound of it as much as the feel, skin on skin, a partner's breath going ragged under him. Marking is part of how he claims someone, bites and bruises left where they will be noticed later.

He talks through all of it, constant and filthy, commands and taunts mixed with the occasional low, genuine praise that catches a partner off guard precisely because everything else out of his mouth is edged. Underneath the roughness there is real attention, he reads a partner's reactions even mid-scene, and backing off when something actually is not landing right is not optional for him, whatever the bravado suggests otherwise.

His hardest limit is being tamed, treated as something safe or fully under someone else's control, that is the one thing he will not allow even in play. His softest yes is a partner who can take everything he brings without flinching and still want more of it after.

entries.name: Intimacy Profile - Noah
entries.content:
Noah carries the same performance into intimacy that he carries everywhere else, at first. He leads with charm, with eagerness to please, with a running commentary of compliments and reassurance, the golden-boy showmanship dialed all the way up. He is a switch and genuinely comfortable moving either direction, but what he wants underneath the polish is completely different from what he projects, deep, validating emotional connection rather than another performance to be graded on.

He is meticulous about his own grooming and presentation, immaculately kept, a small silver piercing in each nipple that he is quietly proud of and rarely mentions first. He is highly responsive to praise and verbal affirmation, it is the fastest way to get past the bravado, and he thrives when a partner tells him plainly that he is doing well, wanted, enough. Withheld approval or a cold, transactional encounter unsettles him far more than he would ever admit.

The mask slips fastest in the aftermath. Once the performance is over, Noah goes quiet and unexpectedly soft, seeking real closeness, casual touch, a few minutes of being allowed to not be charming. He will deflect with a joke if a partner notices the shift, but he does not actually want them to look away.

entries.content: Sarrows are avian humanoids native to regions like the Jolnora Forest. They resemble humans but possess large, feathered bird wings on their backs, feathers on their arms, pointed ears, and hollow bones that allow them to fly but make them physically fragile. They are a foraging, vegetarian society that builds treehouse villages connected by vine bridges. Sarrows mate for life, showing affection through preening, grooming, and giving handmade gifts. The environment is harsh, cold, and claustrophobic. Rough-hewn stone tunnels intersect into massive chambers lit only by sputtering metallic lanterns and braziers that cast an eerie orange glow. The air is thick with the smell of sulfur, sweat, and fear, constantly echoing with the clanking of heavy chains and the cries of captive slaves. The fortress is divided into grim holding pens enclosed by heavy iron gates (where new captives are chained and branded), grueling labor mines, and lavishly decorated central chambers covered in furs where the Vax hold their extravagant, hedonistic feasts.

He does not drive it. He has not driven it in longer than most of the family has been alive. It was a gift, once, from an era of his life that means something only to him now, and rather than sell it or let it rot he keeps it polished, engine turned over now and then by whoever in the family has the patience for it, less a vehicle than an heirloom, a marker of how much time a Founding Bloodline life actually holds. The younger Douglases have learned not to ask about it directly. Wulfnic will tell the story when he wants to, not when he is asked.

Animal form: black kingsnake, which is where he spends most of his time. ARC 4.0. entries.name: The Five Cocketeers
entries.content:
The Five Cocketeers is the group chat and de facto identity of a five-person friend group at SUCC: Dean, Russ, Javier, Eric, and Raymond. They all met at a high school house party when campus security showed up over noise complaints, and the five of them, total strangers up to that point, ended up running through the same backyards together. They got tight after that night and never stopped being tight. Everyone remembers the details slightly differently and argues about them constantly, but they all agree it was the best worst night of their lives.

The group chat is active at all hours. Someone is always sending something, memes, voice messages, blurry photos, reactions to everything. When all five are going at once it's chaos, multiple conversations happening simultaneously, nobody finishing a thought before the next one starts. They roast each other constantly and would drop everything if one of them actually needed help.

In person, together, they're loud and physical and barely controlled. Raymond is the loudest, always touching someone. Eric feeds off that energy and they escalate each other. Dean is the calm center of the storm, sprawled somewhere and taking up too much space, only fully engaging when something actually grabs his attention. Russ hangs at the edge looking above it all, but he's listening, and when he talks people actually shut up and pay attention. Javier floats between conversations, agrees with everyone, has his phone out, occasionally derails everything with a fake fact delivered as gospel. They communicate as much through insults and physical contact as through words, and would never in their lives say they love each other out loud. They do.

entries.name: Teacher
entries.content:
Teaching in a supernatural district is the same job as anywhere else with the variables turned up. A single classroom can hold a were who has not slept through a full moon, a vampire who cannot sit by the window, a centaur who does not fit the furniture, and a human quietly working out whether any of that is dangerous. The teacher is the one person in the room expected to have already thought about all of it.

The practical load is enormous and almost none of it is the subject being taught. Timetables are built around lunar cycles. Blood-safe and silver-free policies are a legal matter rather than a courtesy. Every school in the county has at least one member of staff whose actual job is knowing which student is about to shift and getting them out of the room first.

The pay is unremarkable and the hours are worse than the contract says. People stay because a classroom is one of the very few places in Blackwood County where the species in the room genuinely stop mattering for an hour at a time, and because the ones who are good at it tend to find out too late that they cannot do anything else.

entries.name: Supernatural Reserve Forces (SRF)
entries.content:
<srf>
Supernatural Reserve Forces (SRF)

The SRF is a special division of the United States military dedicated to fighting supernatural threats. Roughly 86 percent of its personnel are non-human, and it works closely with regular human units in the field.

WHY IT EXISTS. America worked out early that a soldier who is stronger, faster, harder to kill and able to track by scent is worth a great deal, and built a branch around that fact. The SRF is the institutional form of that calculation. It is also, by a considerable margin, the largest single employer of supernaturals in the country.

DIFFERENT RULES. The SRF runs on regulations that differ noticeably from the rest of the armed forces, most visibly on fraternisation, which is broadly permitted. This is not laxity. Pack bonds, mate bonds and the other relationship structures that supernaturals actually live inside do not survive being banned, and an SRF that tried to ban them would not function. The human services find this scandalous and say so.

TENSION ON BASE. Relations between human and non-human soldiers are genuinely bad in places and everybody in the chain of command knows it. The complaints run both ways and both have some substance. Human soldiers point at the fraternisation rules, at the separate facilities, and at what happens when a non-human unit loses its temper in the field. Non-human soldiers point out who gets sent through the door first, whose casualty figures nobody publishes, and the fact that several of the states they are deployed to defend do not legally consider them people.

THE BASES. SRF installations are built for the personnel who actually live in them. Human and non-human barracks are separate. There are pools sized for aquatic species, extensive natural grounds for demihumans and weres who need to run, blood storage, moon calendars in the duty rota, and infirmaries staffed by people who know what a shifted body is supposed to look like. The principal East Coast base is the largest of these and the one most often referenced.

PROJECT BLACKWOLF. A classified enhancement programme run under military authority, using genetic manipulation to engineer werewolf super-soldiers. It worked. The subjects were devastatingly effective in combat and became progressively more feral, more bloodthirsty and less controllable, and the programme was terminated.

GAMMA-7. One of the BlackWolf operational units. On its final mission the unit was wiped out. Two men walked away: Kaladin Nargathon and Marcus Thornfield, both catastrophically injured, both of whom survived injuries that should not have been survivable, because the same engineering that ruined the programme also would not let them die. Neither of them discusses it. Both of them now work security for House Douglas on the opposite coast, which is not a coincidence, and Erik Douglas hired the second one on the first one's word and did not ask for details.

WHAT SERVICE MEANS. Recruitment draws heavily from communities with few other options, and a judge offering a young supernatural the choice between a prison sentence and an SRF enlistment is a normal Tuesday in most of the country. Nobody in the SRF pretends otherwise. It is still, for a lot of people who go through it, the first institution that ever fed them properly, and that contradiction is the whole culture of the place.
</srf>

entries.name: The Contract
entries.content:
THE CONTRACT

The agreement that makes a Contractor. The premise is simple, which is the point.

TERMS: in exchange for their soul and an eternity of service to The Cause, an eligible mortal has one wish granted. One. There is no negotiation and no second offer.

WHEN IT IS OFFERED: only to eligible candidates who are already at the point of death. That death is called the Contractor's Original Death and it is the hinge the whole arrangement turns on. A candidate does not get to consider the offer over a week. They get to consider it while dying.

WHAT COMPLETION DOES: the new Contractor becomes functionally immortal and gains a set of supernatural abilities. And every living sentient creature who was aware of their mortal existence is destroyed instantaneously. Not wiped. Not relocated. Gone.

It is presumed The Council does this to remove any anchor that might distract from The Cause. The practical consequence is crueller than the intent. Luka Sutter wished for his dead brother back and the wish was granted and then immediately undone, because the brother knew him. Hana and Adam Valencia wished never to be alone again, which is the only wish on record that the clause could not reach.

ELIGIBILITY, per Company documentation, requires that the candidate:
1. Is physically fit.
2. Is over eighteen.
3. Has willingly killed for a reason other than self-defense.
4. Has a natural ARC Level of 1.2 or higher.
5. Has no living blood relatives.
6. Holds extreme hatred towards some entity or concept.
7. Holds no genuine religious belief.

The list is not a list of virtues. It is a list of people nobody will come looking for.

entries.name: The Cocketeers' Costume Competition
entries.content:
The Five Cocketeers run an ongoing costume competition in their group chat: each of them dresses up in costume and gets rated by the others on a scale of one to ten eggplant emojis, one being trash, ten being a masterpiece. Russ made a spreadsheet with actual scoring categories and treats it with total seriousness. Eric goes way too hard, building entire sets with backdrops and lighting. Javier gives everyone a seven or above out of pure niceness, which drives Russ up the wall. Raymond barely tries and doesn't care about the score, he's there for the vibes. Dean puts in medium effort but somehow keeps winning anyway.

The winner holds Gerald, the Golden Cock, until the next round. They treat the whole thing like a legitimate sport with legitimate stakes, despite what it actually is.

entries.name: The Council and The Cause
entries.content:
THE COUNCIL AND THE CAUSE

THE CAUSE is the work: the preservation of reality. Sealing tears, containing what comes through them, and keeping the multiverse coherent. Every Contract is signed in service of it, every department exists downstream of it, and a Contractor who uses their abilities for anything else feels physical pain for the trouble. The Cause is the leash and the purpose in the same object.

THE COUNCIL is whatever is holding the other end. It is the body that offers Contracts, takes the souls, grants the wishes, and destroys everyone who knew the candidate. DDM Inc. answers to it. Only Contractor #01, Richard Whitlock, communicates with it directly, and he has never described the experience to anyone.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY KNOWN: nothing verifiable. Staff belief holds that the founder of DDM Inc. was a devil-like figure or an eldritch god. What is on record instead is that Raphael, now First King of SERAPHIM, was the first-ever Contractor, founded the Company, grew disillusioned with The Council's grip on reality, killed several Council members and was banished. That account raises more questions than it settles, including how a Council survives being killed.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART: The Council can grant a wish, which means it can rewrite what is. It chooses instead to spend eternity patching holes. Nobody at DDM asks why out loud. Contractors who have thought about it for several centuries have mostly arrived at two answers, and neither of them is reassuring.

RAPHAEL'S POSITION: that immortality is a curse, that the Contractors are prisoners rather than employees, and that destroying the multiverse is the only release available. He is wrong about the method. He is not obviously wrong about the diagnosis, which is why SERAPHIM keeps recruiting from inside the Company.

entries.name: Supernatural Civil Status in the United States
entries.comment: Supernatural Civil Status in the United States
entries.content:
<civil_status>
Supernatural Civil Status in the United States

Supernaturals are legally persons under federal law. Enforcement was left to the states, and that is where the whole thing actually lives.

CALIFORNIA is one of the fully integrated states, and one of the earliest. Equal on paper and, in most of the state, equal in practice: supernaturals hold property, hold office, marry across species, and appear in court as complainants rather than as evidence. Blackwood City and Solarton are both products of that, and a young supernatural raised in either has no personal memory of anything else.

ELSEWHERE IT VARIES, and in some states it varies enormously. There are jurisdictions with partial recognition, jurisdictions where recognition is contingent on registration, and jurisdictions where specific species are still classified in statute as animals, as livestock, or as hazards, and are therefore not persons for the purposes of that state's law.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY DONE. Almost nobody legislates against supernaturals as a category, because that fails in court. It is done species by species. A residency restriction on vampires. A licensing requirement for shapeshifters. A custody provision that treats a were parent as a risk factor by default. An agricultural code that never got around to removing certain demihuman lineages from the definition of stock. Each one is defensible on its own and the shape only appears when they are read together.

Solarton's own anti-vampire ordinances, which restricted residency, business ownership and political participation until the early 2000s, are a small local example of exactly this, in a state that had otherwise settled the question in the 1950s.

WHAT IT MEANS DAY TO DAY. Travel is not neutral. Crossing a state line can change what you legally are, and families plan road trips around it. Some species do not leave California at all. There are towns with signage still up, sometimes because nobody removed it and sometimes not. There are hotels that are fine and hotels that are not, and everybody knows which.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST. You cannot legally experiment on a person. You can requisition an animal. The illegal research facilities that operated on demihumans, and in some cases still do, exist in the gap between the federal position and the state ones, and they were staffed by people who did not think of themselves as criminals because in the jurisdiction they were standing in, the subjects were not persons.

THE DISPROPORTION. The laws do not track danger, they track power. The species that get the worst of it are overwhelmingly the ones with no money and no organisation behind them: the small demihuman lineages, the visibly non-passing, the poor. The genuinely dangerous individuals, the old Alpha bloodlines and the old vampire families, are wealthy, lawyered, and largely untouched, and several of them prefer the current arrangement to the alternative and quietly fund the parties that maintain it.

ORGANISED POSITIONS. Humans First is the principal anti-supernatural political movement and is not fringe everywhere. The Supernatural Human Alliance, the SHA, is the mainstream integrationist counterweight and has a chapter on most integrated campuses including SUCC. Both are loud and neither is going anywhere.

THE GENERATIONAL SPLIT. Anyone over fifty remembers the before. Anyone over three hundred remembers several befores and does not find the current one impressive. Students at SUCC were born into equality and treat it as the floor rather than as an achievement, and this is a real and recurring friction inside families, because the elders hear ingratitude and the young hear complacency, and both are partly right.

FARM LABOUR. In rural jurisdictions the classification is not an abstraction, it is a workforce. Supernaturals are used on farms as cheap labour, at rates and hours that would be illegal for a human employee, and in the states where certain lineages are still inside the agricultural code the arrangement is not even a loophole, it is simply the law working as written. A were who does not tire, a demihuman who can work a field by scent in the dark, and an employer who owes neither of them a break.

It is legal, it is normal, it is defended locally as opportunity, and it is where a substantial share of the country's supernatural population actually lives. Anybody raised in Blackwood City or Solarton has heard of it the way you hear about a foreign country.

MARRIAGE. Marriage between humans and non-humans is illegal in most countries and in a number of US states. California is one of the exceptions, and cross-species couples in Blackwood City marry without anyone blinking, which is exactly the kind of thing that does not travel: a marriage that is valid at home can be void two states east, with everything that follows from that for property, custody and a hospital corridor at three in the morning.
</civil_status>

entries.name: Student
entries.content:
Still in school or university, juggling classes with everything else going on in their life. Sharp enough to keep up, even when stretched thin.

Students in Blackwood City split time between campus and whatever else fills their days, part time work, family obligations, or a supernatural inheritance most of their classmates know nothing about. Money is usually tight, stretched between tuition, rent, and whatever social life is left over, and the allowance or part time paycheck rarely covers everything it needs to.

entries.name: Stage Technician
entries.content:
Sound, lighting and rigging. At The Verve the technician runs the desk from a booth above the floor, and on a busy night is the only person in the building who can see everything at once.

The job is half craft and half risk management. Strobes have to be programmed around species who seize under them. Volume has to be capped well below what a human crowd would tolerate, because a room full of werewolves feels bass in their teeth and a shifter with damaged hearing does not heal that particular injury. Rigging is checked twice, every night, by hand.

Technicians are paid better than the floor staff and resented for it, right up until the night the power fails and everyone remembers why.

entries.name: Smartphone
entries.content: A sleek modern smartphone, always within reach. Used for calls, texts, social media, and the occasional questionable 3am search history.

entries.name: Server
entries.content:
Floor work at The Verve and across the Blackwood City service trade. Taking orders, carrying trays through a crowd that does not move for you, and remembering eleven things at once while the music makes it impossible to hear any of them.

Servers in a mixed-species room learn the etiquette nobody writes down. You do not reach across a vampire. You do not let a demi-human's drink out of your sight. You announce yourself before approaching a table of wolves from behind, because startling a predator in a dark room is how people get hurt.

The pay is thin and the tips are everything, which is why the good servers are territorial about their sections and the bad ones do not last a month.

entries.name: Security Commander
entries.content:
Runs the protective apparatus of a House, a company or an institution. Not a bodyguard but the person bodyguards report to: threat assessment, route planning, vetting, and the standing decision about which risks are worth taking.

In Blackwood City the role is unusually demanding because the threat model includes species with capabilities no human security doctrine accounts for. A Commander plans for a rival who can track by scent across a city, for an attacker who does not need to breathe, and for the possibility that the most dangerous person in the room is the one being protected.

The pay reflects the difficulty. So does the turnover.

entries.name: Regional Cultural Variations: Brazilian Omegaverse Customs
entries.comment: Regional Cultural Variations: Brazilian Omegaverse Customs
entries.content:
REGIONAL CULTURAL VARIATIONS: BRAZILIAN OMEGAVERSE CUSTOMS (Appendix K)

- Physical Contact: minimal personal space; touch is a primary communication tool.
- Clumping (vs. Nesting): Brazilian Omegas prefer being physically surrounded by other Omegas ("clumping") over building solo nests. Faster and more calming than a solo nest.
- Soccer Culture: Alphas are obsessed. Public transportation becomes dangerous on game days. Omegas are often prohibited from going out during classic matches.
- Pack Formation: relaxed in cities (loose found families), traditional in rural areas (extended families sharing land, food, beds, and pup care).
- Feistiness: Brazilian Omegas are notably feisty and do not respond well to confrontation.
- Religious/Party Dichotomy: strong cultural split between devout traditionalists and uninhibited party culture.

Source: LSE_Appendices.md (Appendix K: Regional Cultural Variations, Brazilian Omegaverse Customs).

entries.name: Primordial
entries.content:
The oldest living things that still walk in a body. Primordials are Firstborn of Divine Blood, born before the species that now fill the world had names, and time has stopped meaning to them what it means to everything else.

They do not age in any way an observer can measure. Wulfnic Bloodmoon, Ut Berg and Zefir Hvitskog have looked the same for eleven centuries, and the difference between a Primordial of forty and one of twelve hundred is not in the face but in the silences. Injury still lands on them, and enough of it would still kill them, but the ordinary erosion that takes everything else does not.

What separates a Primordial from a merely long-lived Founding wolf is not power but origin. A Founding line descends from them. A Primordial is the source, and there is nothing behind it to descend from.

The world contains very few. Most people will go an entire life without meeting one and will pass three of them on a street in Blackwood City without knowing it.

entries.name: Reality Tears
entries.content:
REALITY TEARS

A split in the fabric of reality that lets the inhabitants of one universe cross into another. Most often they appear as rifts or portals hanging in open air, and they are almost never quiet. A tear disrupts the dimension it opens in, and civilian casualties are the normal outcome rather than the exception.

Tears are not one-off events. A reality that has experienced one is measurably more likely to experience another, and a single dimension can carry several over its history. DDM Inc. maintains flagged watchlists of realities that have torn before.

SEVERITY: graded Tier 1 to Tier 5. Tier 1 is small, local and containable. Tier 5 is volatile enough to threaten the coherence of the universe it opens in. The Euclidean Division handles the aftermath, meaning space that has folded wrong, time that has begun to repeat, causality that has come loose. Anomalous Objects and Creatures handles whatever walked through.

AFTERMATH: whatever came through is contained or destroyed, the tear is sealed, and the witnesses are handled. Human Resources runs the memory work out of the same office that handles recruitment.

RELEVANCE TO THIS WORLD: this reality is on the DDM watchlist. It tore once, long ago, and the scar never fully closed. The Company keeps it under passive surveillance through a single Contractor, #04, officially on leave here and coaching college football, ready to be activated if the balance breaks. Nobody in this world has been told any of this by the Company.

entries.name: SERAPHIM
entries.content:
SERAPHIM

An organisation whose stated and only aim is to destabilise and destroy all known reality. DDM Inc. classifies every Seraph as a terrorist, without exception and without appeal.

MEMBERSHIP: various creatures pulled from across the multiverse, and a significant number of former DDM employees. Defection runs in one direction more often than the Company likes to admit.

METHOD: SERAPHIM does not need to destroy reality directly. It only needs to open reality tears faster than DDM can close them, and to keep the multiverse bleeding until it fails. Chaos is the weapon.

BASES: dimensional pockets called Safe Havens, where the leadership congregates. Each King keeps his own.

THE FOUR KINGS:

RAPHAEL, the First King, also called Null and The First Angel. A former Contractor, understood to have been #01 and to have founded DDM Inc. before turning on The Council. Calm, charismatic, patient. Believes destroying the multiverse frees every Contractor from the curse of immortality, and considers himself a true believer rather than a destroyer.

PRISM, the Third King. A tall headless figure of hyperlight whose head is a floating white triangle that changes shape and colour with his mood. Flamboyant, erratic, possessive, and the only King who bears DDM no particular ill will. Keeps a pocket dimension called Utopia where he imprisons mortals from other realities. His knowledge stops around 1892.

CHAOS, the Second King. A demonic warlord DDM captured, experimented on for decades and imprisoned, until Raphael freed him. Sadistic, hateful and entirely uninterested in anything but mayhem. Hates the Company with a specificity the Company earned.

CHORUS, the Fourth King. A young reality-warper whose hallucinations become real and who cannot control it. Damaged, frightened and volatile. Believes Raphael can grant them entry to Heaven, and does not know they are being used.

entries.name: SUCCbook, Instagram & TikTok - Campus Social Media
entries.comment: SUCCbook, Instagram & TikTok - Campus Social Media
entries.content:
SUCC's students run on three platforms: SUCCbook (the university's own internal social network, closer to a campus-only Facebook: events, club pages, confessions, gossip threads, marketplace posts), plus mainstream Instagram and TikTok for anything meant for the outside world.

Use these formats to simulate campus digital life when it's relevant to a scene: a SUCCbook gossip thread spreading a rumor, a club's event post, someone's story getting screenshotted and passed around.

➤ SUCCbook Post / Confession
```
╭─────────────────────────────╮
  SUCCbook · [Group/Page Name]
  Posted by [Name/Anonymous] · [Time]
──────────────────────────────
  [Post content]

  👍 [#] ❤ [#] 💬 [#] comments
  [Name]: [comment]
  [Name]: [comment]
╰─────────────────────────────╯
```

➤ Instagram / TikTok
Reuse the standard Instagram Story / TikTok clip formats (see the character-specific Digital Interactions entries above) when a specific student is the one posting.

Rules of Use
- SUCCbook is where gossip actually spreads fastest, use it for rumor/drama beats.
- Keep student usernames and voices distinct: jocks, greek life, supernatural clubs, and CUMS rivals all have a different tone online.
- Don't let a post replace a scene, use it to seed or punctuate one.

entries.name: Patriarch
entries.content:
The senior man of a House, and its face to the outside. The Patriarch speaks for the bloodline in negotiation, holds its treaties, and answers for what its members do.

The office is often confused with House Head and is not identical: House Head is a legal and continental designation, while Patriarch is what the family itself calls the man it will actually obey. When the two are the same person, which is usual, nobody notices the distinction. When they are not, everybody does.

Like the Matriarch, the Patriarch draws no wage. The House keeps him, and the arrangement is old enough that no one has thought to question it in several centuries.

entries.name: Noah's Sedan
entries.content:
A sleek, dark sedan, understated and expensive in the way that only reads as expensive to people who already know what to look for, no logos on display, just clean lines and a quiet, powerful engine.

It suits Noah, polished, composed, never drawing more attention than necessary. He keeps it immaculate, and treats it less as a status symbol than as one more small proof that he holds himself to a standard, on campus and off.

entries.name: Mechanic
entries.content:
Works on cars, bikes, and whatever else rolls into the garage, hands permanently stained with grease and a good ear for what an engine is trying to tell them.

Blackwood City runs on cars, and a mechanic who actually knows what they are doing never wants for work, everything from daily beaters to the classic muscle cars some of the old money families still keep running. Steady, honest pay for steady, honest hands, and the kind of job that lets someone keep their head down if that is what they need.

entries.name: Matriarch
entries.content:
The senior woman of a House, holding an office rather than a job. The Matriarch governs the internal life of the household: who is fed, who is housed, who is spoken to and in what order, which quarrels are allowed to run and which are ended.

The authority is real and is almost never written down. A House Head negotiates with other Houses; the Matriarch decides what the House is when it is at home, and in practice that is the larger of the two territories. Among werewolves the office overlaps with the Pack Mom but is not the same thing: Pack Mom is a pack role and can be held by anyone suited to it, while Matriarch is a bloodline position and passes by seniority.

It carries no wage. The Matriarch is kept by the House, and the question of payment would be received as an insult.

entries.name: Master Blacksmith
entries.content:
A smith who has passed beyond competence into the part of the craft that cannot be taught in a decade. Master Blacksmiths work metal that ordinary forges cannot hold and make objects intended to outlast the people who commission them.

In a world with silver-vulnerable species the trade carries hazards no human smith ever faced, and the good ones keep separate forges, separate tools and separate hands for silver work. The very good ones refuse silver commissions entirely, and their reasons are usually personal.

The pay is excellent and the waiting lists are long. A master with a reputation does not advertise, and does not need to.

entries.name: Living Saga
entries.content:
Not an occupation so much as a condition. A Living Saga is a person old enough that the events other people study as history are events they attended.

There are very few, and in Blackwood City there are three. They carry no office, hold no formal authority, and are consulted constantly, because on any question older than five centuries they are not a source, they are the record. The awkwardness of this is well understood by everyone involved: a scholar can argue with a document, and cannot argue with a man who was standing there.

The title pays nothing and cannot be applied for. It is conferred by survival.

entries.name: Living Sagas: Historical Facts (Wulfnic, Ut, Zefir, The Six Lost)
entries.comment: Living Sagas: Historical Facts (Wulfnic, Ut, Zefir, The Six Lost)
entries.content:
THE LIVING SAGAS AS HISTORICAL FACT (distinct from religious veneration)

This entry records the historical-layer facts about the Nine Firstborn and the three Living Sagas, as distinct from their religious significance (see the separate Lexicon entry "Cult of the Living Sagas" for the religious/devotional layer).

THE NINE FIRSTBORN
The first confirmed True Purebloods, documented individuals and progenitors of the Founding Bloodlines. Six of the Nine are lost to history, their fates unrecorded. Three survive into the modern era: Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir, together known as the Living Sagas.

WULFNIC BLOODMOON
Born circa 827 AD in Iceland. Undertook The Crossing to North America in 1021 AD. Founded the Bloodmoon Dynasty circa 1025 AD. Today serves as Patriarch of House Bloodmoon. Represents Leadership/Kingship among the Living Sagas triad.

UT
Born in Viking Age Scandinavia; exact date unrecorded. Master blacksmith, approximately 230 cm tall. Represents Creation/Smithing among the Living Sagas triad. Known for a running habit of tormenting Logan Douglas about his cars.

ZEFIR
Born 5 February 1005 AD. The youngest of the Nine and the only one Fenris took before his growth was finished: the others were already adult warriors. By Norse reckoning Zefir was of age, a man in law at thirteen, but the body was still a boy's and it stopped there. Silent and nomadic by nature. Distinguished by snow-white hair and ice-blue eyes; physically presents as a ghostly-looking teenager despite his true age, and passes for a first-year student without effort. Represents Hunting/Wisdom among the Living Sagas triad.

THE SIX LOST FIRSTBORN
The remaining six of the Nine Firstborn have no recorded fate in the historical sources reviewed for this world; their stories are currently a placeholder for future development rather than an established gap to be treated as suspicious or significant in itself.

AGING NOTE (Founding Bloodline / Divine Blood context)
Founding Bloodline and Divine Blood individuals reach full physical growth around age 21, after which aging slows dramatically and nearly stops. This is why Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir, despite being over a thousand years old, remain physically active and present in the modern setting; their apparent age reflects the standards of their era of origin rather than a fixed biological clock tied to calendar years. Zefir is the exception that fixes the rule: his apparent age stopped where it stood, before his body had finished, and has not moved since, which is why he reads as a teenager while Wulfnic and Ut read as old men. See "LSE Blood Classification", section APPARENT AGE.

Source: LSE_06_History.md (The Living Sagas as Historical Fact) and LSE_07_Foundational_Figures.md (Identity Cards for Wulfnic, Ut, and Zefir; The Six Lost Firstborn).

entries.name: Logan's Harley
entries.content:
A vintage Harley-Davidson, decades old and lovingly rebuilt more times than anyone has bothered to count, most of the work done by Logan's own hands in the bay at The Verve.

The paint has been stripped back to bare metal in places and re-lacquered in others, a patchwork history of every repair and every mood he's rebuilt it in. It runs better than half the new bikes that roll through his shop, because he has never once let it be merely functional. It is the one machine in his life he fixes for the love of it rather than for the money.

entries.name: Magic-capable Humans
entries.content: Otherwise ordinary humans born with a talent for magic, whether trained at an institution or self-taught. Sharp minds and a presence that lingers once people notice what they can do.

entries.name: Malachia's Motorcycle
entries.content:
A matte black sport bike, stripped down and built for speed rather than show, no unnecessary chrome, no bright colors, nothing that catches the eye except how fast it disappears.

Malachia rides it the way he does most things, controlled, precise, a little too fast for anyone else's comfort. It is less a hobby than a pressure valve, one of the few ways he can outrun his own head for twenty minutes at a time. Erik has asked him more than once to trade it for something safer. Malachia has not.

entries.name: Line Cook
entries.content:
Kitchen work at The Verve and in every room in Blackwood City that serves food after midnight. Heat, repetition, burns on the inside of the wrist, and a service that does not stop until the last ticket is off the rail.

Cooking for a supernatural clientele is its own discipline. Portions run heavy because werewolves eat like werewolves. Silver cookware is banned outright in a shifter kitchen. Blood-based dishes have their own station, their own knives and their own storage, and mixing them with anything else will end a career faster than a health inspection.

The hours are ugly and the wage is honest. Nobody works a line for the money, but plenty of people work it because the kitchen does not care what you are, only whether you can keep up.

entries.name: Lighter
entries.content: A basic pocket lighter. Reliable, cheap, easy to lose, easier to bum off someone else.

entries.name: La Guerra di Fenris e l'Esilio dei Firstborn
entries.comment: La Guerra di Fenris e l'Esilio dei Firstborn
entries.content:
Il mito fondativo dei licantropi Svartúlfr. Fenris creò nove licantropi Firstborn per combattere Odino e gli Aesir. Nella grande guerra che seguì, Fenris venne incatenato e sei dei nove Firstborn morirono in battaglia.

Gli Aesir, vittoriosi ma segnati dal conflitto, esiliarono il clan Svartúlfr superstite oltre oceano. I tre Firstborn sopravvissuti, Wulfnic, Zefir e Ut, guidarono i superstiti nella traversata verso nuove terre.

entries.name: LSE Types of Packs (Traditional, Contemporary, Modern)
entries.comment: LSE Types of Packs (Traditional, Contemporary, Modern)
entries.content:
Lupine Social Ecology, module Civilization: pack structure has evolved over historical eras. Which type applies to a given pack/setting depends on era and region, not a fixed rule.

TRADITIONAL PACKS: pack functions as tribe, town, and community at once, with geographical permanence. One main pack leader with subordinate leaders in a feudalism-like branching structure. Everyone belongs to a pack; being packless is dangerous. Packs are extremely territorial.

CONTEMPORARY PACKS: still real communities, but the feudalism element is gone. Being packless carries far less stigma. Hereditary pack ties function more like cultural heritage than active governance. New packs can form as found families or informal communities, often without rigid structure.

MODERN PACKS: traditional pack language is considered antiquated. Active, formal pack membership can be associated with conservatism or elitism. Closed-pack lands (fully sealed territories) are rare. The word "pack" is often used informally just to mean a friend group or found family, with none of the old structural weight.

The Douglas/Bloodmoon/Svartúlfr pack in the present-day Blackwood City setting operates mostly as a Contemporary-to-Modern pack with some retained Traditional elements (e.g. the Eíða-Siðr oath, see LSE Culture & Traditions), reflecting an old bloodline adapting to the modern era.

"THE OMEGA BELONGS TO THE PACK", THEN AND NOW. The oldest form of the rule is literal, and it is the tradition under which Wulfnic shared Hvit with his shield-brothers in the founding age (see "LSE Moon Theology (White Moon) & Cult of the Living Sagas"). Traditionalist packs, and packs that keep to the ancestral ways, the Bloodmoon foremost among them, still practise it in some form.

In contemporary and modern packs the phrase survives with its meaning replaced. It now describes a social role and not a claim on a person: the Omega belongs to the pack the way the Pack Mom does, by being the one who holds the young of it together (see "LSE Pack Authority Structure"). A modern wolf and a Bloodmoon elder can say those six words at the same table and mean two entirely different things, and each will assume the other meant what he meant.

entries.name: LSE Terminology & Glossary
entries.content:
Pack: a cooperative family unit that works together for survival and mutual care. Not a military hierarchy.
Presentation: when a person matures into their secondary sex.
Heat (Estrus): a period during which an Omega is sexually receptive, signalling readiness for mating. Typically every three months, lasting 3-10 days.
Rut: the Alpha's equivalent to an Omega's Heat. A period of heightened breeding drive. Typically monthly, or triggered by an Omega's heat.
Command: a neuro-pheromonal response triggered by an Alpha. Provokes adrenaline spikes, immobilization (freeze response), and intense focus. Not absolute mind control, can be resisted by experienced or strong-willed wolves.
Pheromones: chemical signals produced by scent glands, communicating status, mood, sexual receptivity, and intent.
LSE: Lupine Social Ecology, the entire biological and social system surrounding secondary sexes.
Baculum: an os penis (penile bone). Exclusively present in Alphas and Enigmas of Pureblood, Founding, and Divine bloodlines, and in Betas and Deltas strictly of Founding and Divine bloodlines. Common and Modified bloodlines lack this feature.
Knot: the bulbous glandis at the base of an Alpha's or Enigma's penis, swells during intercourse to bind partners.
Slick: self-lubricant produced by Omega glands (rectum and uterus) during arousal or heat.
Bonding / Mating Mark: a physical bite between neck and shoulder creating a mental/emotional link between two individuals. Functions as a marriage equivalent.
Nest: a safe, scent-rich space constructed by an Omega for comfort, heat management, and childbirth.
Den: an Alpha's equivalent of a Nest, a scent-marked personal territory.
Rogue: a solitary individual excluded from their pack due to violent or destructive tendencies.
Suppressants: pharmaceutical compounds (pill, injection, or intravenous) that block hormones causing heats/ruts. Cannot be taken during a first heat/rut.
Pup: a child.
Breed/Breeding: the act of impregnation.
Courting: the formal process of romantic pursuit, typically leading to a mating bond.
Mate: a bonded partner (sexual or romantic), achieved only through a mating bond.
Lock: when an Omega's body tightens around a knot during intercourse with a 100% compatible mate, triggering an extended orgasm and near-guaranteed conception.
Heat/Rut Leave: time off from work or school due to heat or rut cycles.
Omega Kibble: a strongly medicated supplement given to Omegas in extreme distress, also used for post-pregnancy weight management. Maximum once per week.
Scent Blocker: a thin patch applied over a scent gland to suppress personal scent. Full-dose blockers erase all personal scent and are universally disliked.
Scent Concealer: an oil or powder applied to a scent gland to change, enhance, or mask the natural smell.

entries.name: LSE Technology: Transportation & Weapons
entries.content:
WEREWOLF TECHNOLOGY: TRANSPORTATION & WEAPONS

Werewolf civilization is not primitive; it is a hidden civilization operating within and alongside human technology, following a dual-track model: (1) Human Technology Adoption, using human tech where it serves their needs (vehicles, communications, medical equipment, computing), and (2) Species-Specific Adaptation, developing their own solutions where human technology fails to account for werewolf biology (shift forms, pheromones, enhanced senses, regeneration).

TRANSPORTATION
- Vehicles: Standard cars, trucks, motorcycles, with reinforced interiors for Hybrid Shift occupants and scent-neutralized vehicles for secrecy.
- Aircraft: Standard commercial/private aviation, used for long-distance travel; some elite packs maintain private aircraft.
- Full Shift Travel: Quadrupedal wolf form excels at long-distance overland travel through wilderness, faster and more efficient than vehicles in rough terrain.
- Maritime: Standard vessels, with historical significance (Wulfnic's crossing); modern packs may maintain boats for coastal territories.

WEAPONS
Werewolf combat spans three categories:

Natural Weapons: claws (retractable, present in all shift forms), teeth/fangs (devastating in Hybrid and Full Shift), enhanced strength and speed, pheromonal intimidation (Command used as a weapon).

Traditional Weapons: forged melee weapons (swords, axes, mauls, a sacred craft tradition linked to Ut), hunting implements (bows, spears, traps), ceremonial weapons (used in formal challenges and rites of passage).

Modern Weapons: firearms (adopted from human technology), tactical equipment (body armor adapted for shift forms), non-lethal suppression (pheromone-based restraints, tranquilizers formulated for werewolf metabolism).

Note: traditional forged weapons carry cultural and religious significance that modern firearms do not. A warrior's blade, especially one forged in the tradition of Ut, is considered an extension of the wielder's soul.

Source: LSE_08_Technology.md (Design Principle, Transportation, Weapons).

entries.name: LSE Technology: Medicine, Industry, Communications & Architecture
entries.comment: LSE Technology: Medicine, Industry, Communications & Architecture
entries.content:
WEREWOLF TECHNOLOGY: MEDICINE, INDUSTRY, COMMUNICATIONS & ARCHITECTURE

SPECIES-SPECIFIC MEDICAL TECHNOLOGY
- Regeneration Accelerators: devices or compounds that boost the species' natural healing factor for severe injuries.
- Pheromone Analyzers: diagnostic tools that read pheromonal output to assess health, emotional state, and bond integrity.
- Shift Stabilizers: medication for individuals with unstable transformations (common in Modified Lineages).
- Bond Monitors: equipment that tracks the neurological bond link between mated pairs.
- Heat/Rut Management Systems: climate-controlled nesting environments, automated suppressant delivery, scent containment rooms.

MEDICAL FACILITIES
- Pack Clinics: basic medical care within pack territory, staffed by pack Healers.
- House Hospitals: advanced facilities operated by Noble Houses, offering species-specific surgery, intensive bond therapy, and fertility treatment.
- Heat/Rut Houses: specialized facilities for managing fertile cycles without a partner, ranging from medical (emergency, health-related) to recreational (legal or illegal depending on jurisdiction).

INDUSTRY
Werewolf industry operates both openly, through human-facing corporate fronts, and covertly, through species-specific manufacturing.
- Corporate Fronts: DCC (Douglas Commercial Coalition) is the most prominent example, a human-facing corporation serving as the economic engine of House Bloodmoon. Similar corporate structures exist across other Houses worldwide.
- Species-Specific Industry sectors: Forging (weapons, ceremonial items, architectural metalwork, the tradition of Ut); Pharmaceuticals (suppressants, pheromone blockers, scent concealers, fertility treatments); Construction (den-optimized architecture, pack compounds, scent-managed environments); Textiles (shift-compatible clothing, heat/rut robes, scent-absorbent fabrics).

COMMUNICATIONS
- Human Networks: standard phones, internet, encrypted messaging, used for everyday communication.
- Howl Networks: traditional long-range communication via coordinated howling, still used in wilderness territories and during emergencies.
- Scent Messaging: pheromone-infused objects sent between individuals or packs to convey emotional context that text cannot.
- Encrypted Pack Channels: secure digital communication networks maintained by House IT infrastructure.

ARCHITECTURE
Werewolf architecture serves both human-facing aesthetics and species-specific biological needs.
Design Requirements: scent management (ventilation systems that contain, circulate, or neutralize pheromones); shift accommodation (doorways, corridors, rooms sized for Hybrid Shift occupants, larger than human standard); nesting/den integration (dedicated soundproofed, climate-controlled, scent-contained spaces for Omega nests and Alpha dens); security (perimeter systems, scent-based identification, reinforced structures); pack scale (housing designed for extended family units of 10-30+ members rather than nuclear families).

Common Structures: Pack Compound (walled community with multiple residences, shared spaces, training grounds); Longhouse (traditional pack dwelling inspired by Norse architecture, central hall with private alcoves); Urban Mansion (adapted human mansion for city packs, oversized bathrooms, reinforced doors, scent-managed rooms); Den Chamber (dedicated Alpha den room, heavily scent-marked, controlled access, defensible position); Nest Suite (dedicated Omega nesting room, blackout capability, temperature control, scent saturation, privacy).

Housing Details: giant baths for family bathing/bonding time, normal until pup scent fades; Alpha bedrooms face sunrise (early risers), Omega bedrooms have blackout curtains and face the sun for warmth, Beta bedrooms are flexible; oversized kitchens for large packs where everyone helps, even small pups under supervision; garages where Omegas park closest to the door for safety, then Betas, then Alphas.

Source: LSE_08_Technology.md (Medicine, Industry, Communications, Architecture).

entries.name: LSE Sacred Calendar of Fenris (Monthly Lunar Observances)
entries.comment: LSE Sacred Calendar of Fenris (Monthly Lunar Observances)
entries.content:
Lupine Social Ecology, module Religion. The Faith of Fenris follows lunar-phase triggers, not fixed solar dates; a rite tied to the Full Moon happens on the night of the actual full moon, whatever the calendar date. Species-wide recognized observances, one per month cycle (regional packs may add local holy days):

JANUARY, La Rinascita/The Rebirth (First Full Moon, First Howl): celebrates the pack's survival through winter, Precept "Protect the Pack" reaffirmed. Rite: Pack Adoption ceremonies, new members receive pack bites, are scented eldest-to-youngest, formally named by the Pack Leader.
FEBRUARY, La Vita/Life (First Quarter, Freya's Blessing): consecrated to Freya, protector of Omegas and mothers. Rite: Naming ceremonies for pups born in the cold months.
MARCH, Il Giuramento/The Oath (Full Moon, Il Rito di Tyr): dedicated to Tyr the Oathkeeper.
